content: 1. Ivosidenib reduces the levels or effects of lopinavir by altering the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. If co-administration is unavoidable, patients should be monitored for a loss of therapeutic efficacy of lopinavir. 2. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of ixabepilone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be considered. 3. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of lapatinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 4. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of lapatinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be considered. 5. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of larotrectinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. If co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, the larotrectinib dose should be reduced by 50%. Once the CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued for 3–5 half-lives, the prior larotrectinib dose should be resumed. 6. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of larotrectinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be considered. If co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, the larotrectinib dose should be reduced by 50%. The prior dose should be resumed after the CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued for 3–5 half-lives. 7. Lasmiditan increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 8. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of lefamulin by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be considered. Avoid co-administration of lefamulin with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 9. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of lefamulin by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. Avoid co-administration of lefamulin with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 10. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of lemborexant by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 11. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of lemborexant by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be considered. Avoid co-administration of lemborexant with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors. 12. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of leniolisib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Ritonavir also increases leniolisib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 13. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel (intrauterine) by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 14. Lopinavir, levonorgestrel (oral)/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate: Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. Significant changes in estrogen plasma levels may occur, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Non-hormonal contraceptives are recommended. 15. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel (oral) by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 16. Lithium and lopinavir both increase the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be considered. 17. Lorlatinib decreases ritonavir levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Ritonavir increases lorlatinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. If unavoidable, reduce the lorlatinib dose by 25 mg/day. After discontinuation of the strong CYP3A inhibitor for 3 plasma half-lives, increase lorlatinib to the previous dose. 18. Lopinavir increases lorlatinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be considered. If unavoidable, reduce the lorlatinib dose by 25 mg/day. Resume the previous dose after discontinuation of the strong CYP3A inhibitor for 3 plasma half-lives. 19. Ritonavir and lovotibeglogene autotemcel: Discontinue antiretrovirals (ARTs) at least 1 month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. Long-acting ARTs may require a longer discontinuation period for elimination. ARTs may interfere with lovotibeglogene autotemcel manufacturing. 20. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of lurasidone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 21. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of lurbinectedin by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. If unavoidable, reduce the lurbinectedin dose by 50%. After discontinuation of the strong CYP3A inhibitor for 5 half-lives, increase lurbinectedin to the previous dose. 22. Lopinavir increases lurbinectedin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be considered. If unavoidable, reduce the lurbinectedin dose by 50%. Resume the previous dose after discontinuation of the strong CYP3A inhibitor for 5 half-lives. 23. Macimorelin and lopinavir both increase the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. Macimorelin increases the corrected QT interval by approximately 11 msec. Avoid co-administration with drugs that prolong the QT interval, as this could increase the risk of torsade de pointes-type ventricular tachycardia. 24. Lopinavir increases macimorelin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 25. Ritonavir increases macitentan levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. Avoid co-administration of macitentan with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 26. Lopinavir increases macitentan levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be considered. Avoid co-administration of macitentan with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 27. Ritonavir increases medroxyprogesterone levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 28. Ritonavir increases mefloquine levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. Mefloquine may enhance the QTc-prolonging effect of high-risk QTc-prolonging agents. 29. Lopinavir increases mefloquine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be considered. 30. Lopinavir increases mestranol levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 31. Ritonavir increases methylergonovine levels by decreasing its metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 32. Lopinavir increases metaxalone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be considered. 33. Lopinavir increases methadone levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 34. Lopinavir increases methylprednisolone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be considered. 35. Ritonavir increases metoclopramide (intranasal) levels by altering CYP2D6 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. Concurrent use of metoclopramide intranasal and strong CYP2D6 inhibitors is not recommended, as the metoclopramide dose cannot be adjusted. 36. Ritonavir increases midazolam levels by decreasing its metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 37. Lopinavir increases midazolam levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be considered.
